LESSON: READING 5.2.1 READING FOR INFORMATION

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 5
Topic 5.2: Reading 5.2.1 Reading for Information

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Reading 5.2.1 Reading for Information. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: Why is it important to read texts?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. answer direct and inferential questions from a written text

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. answer direct and inferential questions from a written text
   In simple words: practise until you can answer direct and inferential questions from a written text. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Talk about Reading 5.2.1 Reading for Information using something you see at school in Kenya.

Example 2: Give a home example from your county, estate, or village.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Underline two new ideas about Reading 5.2.1 Reading for Information in the examples.
2. Explain Reading 5.2.1 Reading for Information to a parent using one local example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Reading 5.2.1 Reading for Information.
4. Show that you can: answer direct and inferential questions from a written text

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Reading 5.2.1 Reading for Information using examples from school or home.
2. Answer: Why is Reading 5.2.1 Reading for Information important for a Grade 7 learner?
3. Make a one-minute oral presentation to a parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Conduct a reader’s theatre to read a passage on the theme of cultural diversity,
2. Collaborate with peers to identify vocabulary related to the theme and read aloud,
3. Self-efficacy: This is enhanced when the learner shows concerted attention when working jointly to infer the meaning of vocabulary in context.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. answer direct and inferential questions from a written text

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
